content.value_statement: Software projects lose clarity when teams use vague or conflicting terms. This skill helps Claude, Codex, or Claude Code refine glossary entries, context maps, and ADRs.
actual_capabilities: Creates or updates CONTEXT.md when domain terms are resolved.
Uses CONTEXT-MAP.md to locate multiple bounded contexts.
Challenges vague, overloaded, or conflicting project terminology.
Compares domain claims with code when the user asks how behavior works.
Suggests ADRs only for durable, surprising, trade-off driven decisions.
Applies the included CONTEXT.md and ADR formatting guidance.
limitations: It does not replace stakeholder interviews or domain expert review.
It should not store implementation details in CONTEXT.md.
It depends on the repository containing enough code or discussion context.
It writes documentation only when a term or decision is ready.

use_cases.title: Align product language
use_cases.description: Resolve competing product terms and record the chosen language in a project glossary.

use_cases.title: Document architecture decisions
use_cases.description: Capture a durable technical decision in a short ADR when the trade-off matters.

use_cases.title: Map bounded contexts
use_cases.description: Separate domain concepts across ordering, billing, fulfillment, or similar contexts.

prompt_templates.title: Start a glossary
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner prompt for a new or undocumented project.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me create a CONTEXT.md glossary for this project. Ask me about unclear domain terms before writing entries.

prompt_templates.title: Resolve term conflicts
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate prompt when existing language is inconsistent.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the current CONTEXT.md and this feature discussion. Identify conflicting terms and propose canonical names.

prompt_templates.title: Add a context map
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced prompt for repositories with multiple bounded contexts.
prompt_templates.prompt: Model these bounded contexts and create a CONTEXT-MAP.md that explains their relationships and glossary locations.

prompt_templates.title: Decide on an ADR
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced prompt for architecture decision review.
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate this technical decision against the ADR criteria. If it qualifies, draft a concise ADR with the chosen option and reason.

output_examples.input: We use account, customer, and user to mean similar things in the checkout flow.
output: The skill asks which concept owns payment responsibility and which concept authenticates access.
It recommends canonical terms and records avoided synonyms in CONTEXT.md.

output_examples.input: We chose domain events instead of direct service calls between billing and fulfillment.
output: The skill checks whether the decision is durable, surprising, and based on a real trade-off.
It drafts a short ADR only if those criteria are met.

output_examples.input: Our repository has ordering and billing folders with separate domain rules.
output: The skill proposes separate context glossaries and a root context map.
It describes relationships between contexts without mixing implementation details into the glossary.

best_practices: Resolve one term at a time and update documentation immediately.
Use concrete scenarios to test whether definitions are precise.
Keep ADRs short and reserve them for decisions that future readers may question.
anti_patterns: Do not use CONTEXT.md as a specification or implementation notebook.
Do not add general programming terms that are not unique to the domain.
Do not create ADRs for obvious or easily reversible choices.

faq.question: What files does this skill use?
faq.answer: It uses CONTEXT.md, CONTEXT-MAP.md, and ADR files under docs/adr when those files are relevant.

faq.question: Can it create new documentation files?
faq.answer: Yes. It creates them lazily when a term, context, or decision is ready to record.

faq.question: Does it write implementation specifications?
faq.answer: No. It keeps CONTEXT.md focused on domain language and keeps implementation decisions in ADRs.

faq.question: When should I ask for an ADR?
faq.answer: Ask when a decision is hard to reverse, surprising without context, and based on a real trade-off.

faq.question: Can it handle multiple domains in one repository?
faq.answer: Yes. It uses CONTEXT-MAP.md to separate contexts and explain how they relate.

faq.question: Is it useful for non-technical stakeholders?
faq.answer: Yes. It can turn stakeholder language into clear terms that engineers and product teams share.
